name: hexen
title: Hexen (Raven, Watcom C / DOS4GW)
_units: The program's OWN object list, which is better than any list written here: it is the build the authors actually ran. Read from the WHOLE makefile, not just LOCOBJS/GLOBOBJS -- the link rule is `tic.exe : $(LOCOBJS) $(GLOBOBJS) i_ibm.obj`, so the one file holding every machine dependency, and main, is named nowhere else.
_defines: __WATCOMC__ selects the DOS paths; __386__ the flat model. Both are the compiler's own identity macros, and I_IBM.C genuinely needs them -- its externdata_t exists only under __WATCOMC__.
_unitDefines: R_DRAW.C alone is compiled with __WATCOMC__ UNDEFINED. Its inner rendering loops -- R_DrawColumn, R_DrawSpan -- have C bodies behind `#ifndef __WATCOMC__` because Watcom takes them from LINEAR.ASM instead. Same switch as Quake's id386=0: the source ships both and a build selects one. Until PRISM compiles the assembly (P5.2) this is what makes the renderer exist at all.
_caseInsensitive: The tree writes `DoomDef.h` for `DOOMDEF.H`. A case-sensitive filesystem will not forgive that; DOS never had to.
_compile: pack 1 is the makefile's CCOPTS /zp1 -- byte alignment, so EVERY struct in the program changes size. Not a detail: it is the on-disk layout of the game's own saved games and its lump structures.
_blocked: Hexen builds and runs but stops on its OWN data, not on PRISM. P_SETUP.C:803 defaults every map's sky to R_TextureNumForName("SKY1"), and the retail v1.1 WAD has no SKY1 -- 148 textures, SKY2/3/4, no SKY1 (read straight out of the WAD; PRISM's lookup verified exact, SKY2->72, X_WATER4->147, absent->-1). Patching the game or its data is the one thing this project does not do. See ROADMAP P6.2.
